verdict.rationale: PlanetScale documents database branching as isolated development and test environments. Postgres branches can be restored from backups or from a point-in-time timestamp, which gives production-shaped data. Vitess branching is described only as branching schemas, and no evidence shows the branches are instant or copy-on-write; data appears to come from backup restores rather than a live clone. Missing for 10: evidence of instant copy-on-write branching, schema-plus-data cloning without a backup restore, and independent hands-on corroboration of branching speed.

support.subject: As a developer, I can create an instant copy-on-write branch of my database — schema and data — to develop and test against production-shaped data

citations.quote: Branches on PlanetScale Postgres are isolated database deployments that provide you with separate environments for development and testing, as well as restoring from backups.
You can now create a PostgreSQL branch restored to a point-in-time timestamp with --restore-point.
PlanetScale allows you to branch database schemas the same way you branch your code.
You can then create development branches that you can use for development before shipping schema changes to production.
It will give you a database branch for each Git branch and help you manage the workflows around it.
